newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to boost crude imports over coming winter.
newsitem.headline: Romania to boost crude imports over coming winter.

text.p: Romania plans to import some 1.0 million tonnes of crude per month over the coming winter and the country will not face a repeat of the energy crisis it suffered this year, an official said on Tuesday.
"We will import up to 1.0 million tonnes of crude a month in the coming winter months," Mihail Georgescu, general manager of the state Romanian Oil Company (CRP), told reporters.
Georgescu said the programme to increase crude imports was going smoothly due largely to "huge" financial efforts made by the CRP to secure payment in time.
"For the time being, all our outstanding bills have payment deadlines in October. We have no arrears," he said.

Last month, Romania imported 700,000 tonnes of crude, Georgescu said, adding that CRP estimates put October crude imports at 1.18 million tonnes. This was compared with imports of 295,700 tonnes in August.
Georgescu said the CRP had asked the state bank Banca Romana de Comert Exterior Bancorex SA to convert into hard currency 325 billion lei ($97.2 million) to fund the November crude imports.
However, he gave no indication of when Bancorex would do this. The local foreign exchange interbank market has been plagued for months by hard currency shortages.
Up to 68 percent of costs for crude imports would be covered by export earnings from processed products, he said.
Georgescu dismissed rumours in the local media that Romania might suffer a repeat of an energy crisis which hit the country earlier this year.
"We will not have a repeat of that crisis. We hope to avoid any disruptions in crude imports," he said.
An acute shortage of hard currency to pay for fuel imports forced the Renel RA electricity authority to cut power supplies to industrial sectors over January-March.
The government set up a special fund to finance crude imports, to preclude a fresh crisis.
Romania must import large quantities of crude for domestic energy needs and to keep its refineries operating at a minimum.
This month, Romania guaranteed a $200 million loan for crude imports by the CRP. The loan was arranged with Chase Manhattan.
Renel recently said it would spend $160 million to import fuel oil.
